chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Saqafi, from Ali ibn al-Mu'alla, from Isma'il ibn Yasar, from Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Arqam al-Kufi, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

'Whichever family is given their share of kindness, then Allah has expanded for them in sustenance. And kindness in managing one's livelihood is better than abundance in wealth. And kindness is such that nothing is lost from it, and extravagance is such that nothing remains with it. Surely Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is Kind, He loves kindness.'

key_terms.الرِّفْق: Kindness, gentleness, or ease in conduct

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and economic benefit of kindness (rifq) in the family according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni narrates this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking domestic tranquility to divine provision by contrasting the enduring nature of 'rifq' (gentleness) with the depletion of 'tabdhir' (extravagance). The Imam grounds this practical wisdom in the divine attribute of Allah being 'Rafiq' (Gentle), suggesting that familial kindness is a mirror of divine character that invites spiritual and material expansion.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Saqafy, from Ali Bin Al Moalla, from Ismail Bin Yasaar, from Ahmad Bin Ziyad Bin Arqam Al Kufy, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whichever family are given their share from the kindness, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Expand upon them regarding the sustenance, and the kindness during the management of life is better than the capaciousness in the wealth, and the kindness is such that nothing is lost from it, and the extravagance is such that nothing remains with it. Surely, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Kind, He<sup>azwj</sup> Loves the kindness’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allah from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi from Ali ibn Mu’alla from Isma’il ibn Yasar from Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Arqam al-Kufi from a man from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Any family who has received their share of kindheartedness, Allah has certainly increased their livelihood. Friendliness in matters of earning a living is better than great wealth. Friendliness does not cause any weakness but a spendthrift habit leaves nothing in place. Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, is compassionate and He loves friendliness.”
